items.title: The reduced-motion rule turns every site fade into a cut
items.dedupe_of: 11.1.1 row 8 (O-350, reduced motion is a fade); built at faf12109d
items.evidence:
Holds on re-read. Since v11.1.0, master's src changes only fourier-field/constants.ts and composables/glass/backdropLuminanceSample.ts (git diff --stat v11.1.0 master -- src).

On master and v11.1.0, src/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css:45-54 is `@layer components { @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *,*::before,*::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0s !important } } }`, and index.css:1 is `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;`. Under Cascade 5 a layered !important beats every unlayered rule, important or not. Only an inline `!important` or a Web Animation gets past it, so no site stylesheet rule can lift it, as keyframes says.

On the tip d0f85bd29, faf12109d moves it to a11y-overrides.css:20-30: `@layer reduced-motion { … animation-duration: 0.01ms; animation-iteration-count: 1; transition-duration: 0s }`, a normal declaration at zero specificity. index.css:1 is `@layer theme, base, components, utilities, reduced-motion;`. Glass's own surviving fades are !important carves in components (comment at a11y-overrides.css:15-19: reveal.css, dissolve.css, transitions.css; faf12109d also carves expandable-container/styles.css).

Witness: tests-visual/release-11-1-1/reduce-harness.html:9-10 has an unlayered `.site-fade { transition: opacity 144ms linear }` with no !important. release-11-1-1-reduce.spec.ts:107-120 asserts a computed `0.144s` and more than two fading frames. It is R/G in four projects (critique-2.md:64, critique-3.md:72). fix-8.md:116-128 does not name `site`: it is in part D, whose one failure on the tip is the Sheet bottom fade in WebKit 390.

The site keeps its own clock. The 200 ms cap (orchestrator-note-row-8.md:7, not :6) binds glass's carves. The ask's literal mechanism was not adopted. It was not 'ruled out': the note's binding build (:6) keeps the fallback clockless and makes it relaxable.

It reaches keyframes. demo/styles/style.css:1 imports tailwindcss first, so glass's layer list appends `reduced-motion` after `utilities`, and keyframes' SFC and stylesheet CSS is unlayered. Its r1 fade (an unscoped <style>, repair/NOTES.md:12) and the ChannelOptions.vue:543-553 pane cross-fade would keep their clocks on the tip. Its present Web Animation fades (ControlsPaneWrapper.vue:686-730 at 3e54f9c7) are untouched on either tree.

The limit is a utility. TimelineTrack.vue:47 `transition-opacity duration-fast` sits in `utilities`, before `reduced-motion`, so it is still a cut on 11.1.1, as the CHANGELOG says ('Utility classes are still stilled'). A utility lifts it with Tailwind's important flag (`duration-fast!`), because any !important beats the layer's normal declaration. Glass also no longer stills keyframes' own unlayered movement, which keyframes already guards with its own reduced-motion rules (AnimationControlsGroup.css:233-263).
items.cure: Root cause on v11.1.0: the blanket guard is a layered !important (`@layer components`, a11y-overrides.css:45-54), which no unlayered rule can beat. Cure built on the tip at faf12109d: a normal declaration in a last `reduced-motion` layer (a11y-overrides.css:20-30, index.css:1), with glass's own fades as carves. Witness: reduce spec `site` (release-11-1-1-reduce.spec.ts:107), RED on v11.1.0 and GREEN on d0f85bd29 in Chromium and WebKit at 390 and 1440.
items.row: K3 (O-416) is 11.1.1 row 8, built. Nothing to book. Once keyframes is on 11.1.1, an unlayered SFC fade can replace the Web Animation stand-in. Its one utility fade (TimelineTrack.vue:47) needs restating unlayered or with the important flag.
items.reply: Glass 11.1.1 puts the reduced-motion rule in its own last cascade layer as a plain declaration, so your own unlayered or inline rule, such as `transition: opacity 140ms`, keeps its clock under reduced motion without !important. Utility classes are still stilled unless marked important (TimelineTrack's `transition-opacity duration-fast` is one), and the Web Animation stand-in becomes optional.

items.title: A detented Sheet wearing sheet-animate shows its plate again between the exit fade and unmount
items.evidence:
The core holds. `@utility sheet-animate` is btn.css:95-100 on master and v11.1.0, and identical at btn.css:99-104 on the tip. Its out leg is tw-animate-css 1.4.0's `--animate-out: exit … var(--tw-animation-fill-mode,none)`, so it has no fill. It ends at --duration-fast × tempo (0.2s, scheme-motion.css:101) and opacity returns to 1.

The sliding arm writes inline `animation: none` (v11.1.0 SheetContent.vue:167; tip :187). The detented arm does not (v11.1.0 :157; tip :166-173), and nothing else switches it off: there is no animation rule in sheet/styles.css, and useMotionAxis hostStyle only sets --motion-weight. So the keyframe runs while the detents spring holds the mount (tip :193-195; use.ts:187-191).

On v11.1.0 the box stops at its floor (styles.css:543) until the spring settles. On the tip, 22e65f1ba slides it below the floor with the `translate` longhand (styles.css:566-577). That does not clash with the keyframe's `transform` track.

The number recomputes. bloom is response 0.42 and ζ 0.9 (springPresets.ts:106-109), so ω = 14.96 and 1 − x(0.2 s) = e^(−2.693)·(cos 1.304 + 2.065·sin 1.304) = 0.153 of the travel. At a 0.5 rung at 844 that is about 64 px of plate back at opacity 1 at 200 ms, until it is under 1 % on screen at 374-384 ms (critique-6.md:133-135, 345-348). This is a static read.

Under reduced motion on the tip the plate does not pop. leave() fades it on one clock (use.ts:141-160, 217-233, 26e2fea69), and the reduced-motion layer clamps the keyframe to 0.01 ms with no fill.

Correction: the placement's 'one fade on one clock' under reduce is true for the plate and the scrim (:218), not the whole surface. The Sheet's frost is a sibling span, glass-graded-halo (:458-465; backdrop blur 34px × glass-level and a 10-34 % tint, styles.css:365-389). It takes no opacity from the plate in either motion mode. A plate fade, whether sheet-animate's, keyframes' Web Animation or glass's own reduced-motion fade, leaves the frost painted until unmount. keyframes' own film shows it: film-pr2-sheet-close.png, plate faded by 253 ms, frost band still blurring the cube at 253, 315 and 366 ms, gone at 421 ms; r2-sheet-close.png at 293 ms likewise. So filling the plate alone, as placed, still leaves a frost slab through the hold. Its plate-only witness would read GREEN over it.

Scope holds. No exits row or exits-table cell wears sheet-animate. Glass's own wearer, ModalOverlay.vue:81, drops it whenever a spring drives the scrim (:85; SheetContent :350, DialogContent :229). It is a published utility (.published-roster:263) authored for Sheet (CHANGELOG at the tip:5875-5877), so the flash comes from glass's own utility on its documented host.

keyframes wore it at adab14e2 (ControlsPaneWrapper.vue:252) and dropped it at 3e54f9c7. It now fades by a forwards-filled Web Animation (:704-725) plus a plain `[data-leaving] { opacity: 0 }` rule (:959-962). The placement's caution stands. On 11.1.1 under reduce, glass's detented fade starts its inline opacity at 1 (use.ts:148). That inline value beats keyframes' class rule, and only its forwards fill holds 0.
items.cure:
Root cause: the published `sheet-animate` out leg (tw-animate `animate-out`, fill none) ends at --duration-fast while glass's detented spring holds the mount to about 480 ms, and the detented arm, unlike the sliding arm, leaves CSS animations on. The utility also fades only the plate, never its sibling frost sampler.

Smallest cure, all in the utility:
- Add `motion-safe:data-[state=closed]:fill-mode-forwards` (btn.css:99-104). It is gated to motion-safe because a forwards-filled 0.01 ms keyframe under reduce would beat 26e2fea69's inline fade and make it a cut.
- Put the same fade, on the same clock and fill, on the plate's next sibling (`& + [data-slot="glass-graded-halo"]`, the span authored right after the content at SheetContent.vue:458), so the frost leaves with the plate.

No export, token or unchosen default changes. Making the detented exit a fade in normal motion would change the default look (a minor) and is not needed.

Witness: a bottom detented SheetContent with class `sheet-animate`, at 390 touch and 1440, in Chromium and WebKit, closed by the ✕, Escape, an outside press and a flick, filmed per frame in normal motion with both the plate's and the halo's opacity. The halo stays within 0.05 of the plate on every frame. Once the plate reads ≤ 0.02, no later frame before unmount paints either above 0.02.
- RED on v11.1.0: the plate is back to 1 at about 200 ms on the floor stub and the halo holds 1 throughout.
- RED on d0f85bd29: the plate is back to 1 at about 200 ms while sliding, and the halo holds 1.
- GREEN after.

A reduce leg keeps the out leg a monotone fade of at least two frames within 200 ms.
items.row: K4 (O-416): not an 11.1.1 row. The flash needs a consumer-worn public utility, and the tip's claimed detented exit holds for glass's sheet as shipped, so it is not the next fix round. It is a glass defect for 11.1.2, a fill plus a sibling rule on one utility. It is the same sheet as the study's G10 but none of its four parts (triage-1119/PLACED.md:33), and it is separate from critique 6's gap B. The frost sampler left out of glass's own reduced-motion fade is a separate 11.1.1 claim, filed as K4b.
items.reply: Glass 11.1.2 will make `sheet-animate` hold its faded end until a held Sheet unmounts, and carry the sheet's frost layer through the same fade, so nothing shows again after it. Until then your own plate fade leaves glass's frost layer painted until the close (your 253–366 ms frames show it), and under reduced motion on 11.1.1 keep the Web Animation's forwards fill rather than relying on the `[data-leaving]` class rule.

items.title: A Sheet's frost sampler stays whole through its reduced-motion fade, then goes in one frame
items.evidence:
This comes from K4's second half, 'the detented exit is one fade on one clock'. The K4 placement said the tip already does this under reduced motion. A static read of the tip says it does not, for the whole surface.

On the tip, SheetContent.vue writes the reduced-motion fade as inline opacity on the content only:
- detented arm, :166-173 (`opacity: sheetDetents.opacity`);
- sliding arm, :180-189 (`opacity: fade ? 1 - p`).
The scrim takes the fade too (:218: scrimDetentOpacity × opacity).

The Sheet's frost is not the plate. The plate's own backdrop-filter is none (styles.css:361-363), and the frost is a sibling span, glass-graded-halo (:458-465). It is anchored to the plate's box (styles.css:365-389: backdrop blur(34px × glass-level) saturate, a 10-34 % plate-overlay tint, mask 0.325→1). It has no style binding and is mounted exactly while the content is held (haloPresent, :204-207). Nothing hides it under reduced motion: styles.css:462-466 hides it only under reduced transparency or forced colors.

So under reduce on d0f85bd29:
- The halo appears whole on the first frame while the plate fades in.
- It holds full frost while the plate fades out (26e2fea69, use.ts:141-160, 217-233).
- It is removed in one frame with the mount.
This holds for sliding and detented sheets alike. The reduce spec films only the content element (release-11-1-1-reduce.spec.ts:150-152), so its GREEN does not read the halo. No 11.1.1 critique or fix names it.

The frost is visibly there once a plate fades. keyframes' after-repair film on 11.1.0 (FRONTS/keyframes/final/repair/sheets/film-pr2-sheet-close.png, 390 touch) shows its plate faded by 253 ms while a frost band still blurs the cube's lower half at 253, 315 and 366 ms, gone by 421 ms; r2-sheet-close.png at 293 ms the same.

11.1.1 claims this exit. The CHANGELOG paragraph 'Reduced motion is a fade' says sheets fade in and out over at most 200 ms, and 26e2fea69 says the detented Sheet 'fades out where it stands' with the scrim following. The tip read is static, not measured.
items.cure:
Root cause: the Sheet's glass is two boxes, the plate and its sibling frost sampler, and the reduced-motion fade is written on one. Smallest cure: SheetContent writes the same fade value on the halo span. One fade value (detented `sheetDetents.opacity`, sliding `1 - p` under reduce) is read by both springStyle and a `:style` on the span at :458-465.

Witness: the reduce spec's Sheet right, Sheet bottom and detented Sheet cells also film `[data-slot="glass-graded-halo"]`. On every frame it is present, its opacity is within 0.02 of the plate's, and it leaves at ≤ 0.02 and enters from ≤ 0.02. Chromium and WebKit, 390 and 1440.
- RED on v11.1.0: plate and halo both cut.
- RED on d0f85bd29: the halo reads 1 on every frame of the plate's fade and goes in one frame.
- GREEN after.
items.row: New, from K4 (O-416). An exits row 11.1.1 claims (row 8, reduced motion is a fade, with 26e2fea69's detented fade) that the tip fails on a static read, so it goes to the next fix round. It covers sliding and detented sheets. It is not a duplicate of any row in INBOUND O-396 to O-415, triage-1119 or hassio-r13 PLACED, or the 11.1.2 scope (none names the sheet's halo). Critic 8 should film the halo beside the plate. K4's 11.1.2 cure carries the normal-motion half for sheet-animate wearers.
items.reply: Glass 11.1.1 will fade a Sheet's frost layer along with its plate under reduced motion, so no frost is left standing through the fade and cut at the end.

changed: K3: verdict and release hold. Cites corrected: the 200 ms cap is orchestrator-note-row-8.md:7, not :6, and fix-8.md:116-128 places `site` in part D without naming it. 'Ruled out' is restated as 'not adopted'. Added keyframes' one utility fade still stilled on 11.1.1 (TimelineTrack.vue:47) and the important-flag path, plus the check that keyframes' unlayered CSS sits outside glass's layers.

K4: verdict and release hold. Withdrew the claim that the tip makes the detented exit one fade on one clock under reduced motion: the sibling frost sampler (glass-graded-halo) is outside it. keyframes' own films show that sampler outliving a plate fade. The cure now also carries the halo through sheet-animate's fade, since a fill on the plate alone leaves a frost slab through the hold. The witness now films both. The reply no longer calls keyframes' fade-then-close sound without that caveat. Recomputed the 15 % / about 64 px figure, which holds.

K4b: added. The Sheet's frost sampler sits outside 11.1.1's own reduced-motion Sheet fade, so it appears whole and goes in one frame. It is an exits row 11.1.1 claims and the tip fails it on a static read, so it goes to 11.1.1's next fix round.
